preamble: Eight clues produce one of a pair of commonly linked words. Its partner is the required grid entry.

clue.text: Crowd ended exercise

parts.note: to crowd someone is to press them
something ended is up, as in 'time's up'

explanation.surface: A gym crowd has finished a workout.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up is a floor exercise lifting the body on the arms; Americans call it a push-up.

clue.text: Guarantee place advantage

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for Place in street names
an edge is an advantage

explanation.surface: Being sure of a positional advantage.
explanation.definitionFit: A pledge is a solemn promise or a security given as surety.

clue.text: Each year end increase is an obstacle for auditors

indicators.note: end picks out the final letter of year

parts.note: to wax is to grow, as the moon does

explanation.surface: An annual year-end rise is a hurdle for accountants checking the books.
explanation.walkthrough: Auditors here are listeners, not accountants.
explanation.definitionFit: Earwax builds up in the ear canal and can block hearing, so it hinders listeners.

clue.text: Protect game — it could get you on film

definitions.text: it could get you on film

parts.note: to screen is to shield or protect
a test is a test match, an international cricket game

explanation.surface: Guarding a match result might land you in the movies.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen test is an audition filmed to judge an actor's suitability for a role.

clue.text: Grand parrot is celebrity

parts.note: a lory is a small brightly coloured parrot

explanation.surface: A magnificent talking bird has become a star.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives GLORY; its partner in 'power and glory' is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Glory is fame and renown, which is what celebrity means.

clue.text: Live in retreat — most mean

indicators.note: in places the word for living inside the word for a retreat

parts.note: a nest is a snug retreat or hideaway
to live is to be; 'we are' gives ARE

explanation.surface: Someone living as a recluse is called the stingiest of all.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay builds NEAREST; by the preamble its partner in 'nearest and dearest' goes in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Near is an old word for stingy, so the nearest person is the most miserly.

clue.text: Cardinal possibly raised double gun

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is turned upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: cardinal is a red colour, so red is an example of it
a ringer is someone's double, a lookalike

explanation.surface: A churchman lifts a double-barrelled weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small short-barrelled pocket pistol.

clue.text: Bachelors hurt inside

indicators.note: inside says the answer lies within the letters of Bachelors

explanation.surface: Single men nursing an inner wound.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to feel a dull continuous pain, to hurt.

clue.text: Going to pieces on getting into cooking

indicators.note: getting into shows the word for on goes inside the word for cooking

parts.note: baking is cooking in an oven
RE means on or about, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Someone falls apart after taking up cookery.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives BREAKING; its partner in 'breaking and entering' is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Something breaking is shattering, falling to pieces.

clue.text: Playing by ear? Try hybrid fruit

indicators.note: Playing suggests the letters are played about with into a new order

explanation.surface: A musician improvising urges us to sample a crossbred berry.
explanation.definitionFit: The tayberry is a cross between a blackberry and a raspberry, bred in Scotland.

clue.text: Industrialist's housing experiment

indicators.note: housing says the word Industrialist's holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A factory owner's homes are a social experiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives TRIAL; its partner in 'trial and error' is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A trial is a test or experiment run to see what happens.

clue.text: Throw-out before a score? Attempt might pay off

indicators.note: out after Throw signals its letters are put out of order

parts.note: a try is a score in rugby

explanation.surface: A rugby lineout throw before a try: a gamble that could pay off.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is worth a try means the effort may be rewarded.

clue.text: Rapture! Fig cultivated as a possible basis for a fad diet

definitions.text: a possible basis for a fad diet

indicators.note: cultivated suggests the letters of Rapture and Fig are worked over into a new shape

explanation.surface: Joy at a fig grown for the latest slimming fad.
explanation.definitionFit: The grapefruit diet was a well-known slimming craze built around eating the citrus fruit.

clue.text: Underwear ultimately unsuitable for a northern hillside

parts.note: a bra is an item of underwear

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of unsuitable

explanation.surface: Lingerie is no good for walking a Scottish slope.
explanation.definitionFit: Brae is the Scots word for a hillside or steep bank.

clue.text: Knockout stuff from loch or ground

indicators.note: ground means crushed, so the letters are broken and remade

explanation.surface: A sedative drug sourced from a Scottish lake or land.
explanation.definitionFit: Chloroform is a volatile liquid once used as an anaesthetic to render people unconscious.

clue.text: Turn right, then Green St and stay?

indicators.note: Turn tells the solver to turn the letters about into a new order

explanation.surface: Directions: turn right, then into Green Street and wait there.
explanation.walkthrough: A stay is a brace or support, which is why it can define a strengthener.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a rope or strut that braces a mast or structure, so it reinforces it.

clue.text: Use it for a change to cover burn in a religious ceremony

indicators.note: to cover means the jumbled letters wrap around the word for burn
for a change signals the letters of Use and it are changed in order

parts.note: to char is to burn or scorch

explanation.surface: An instruction to treat a burn as part of a church rite.
explanation.definitionFit: The Eucharist is the Christian sacrament of Holy Communion, celebrating the Last Supper.

clue.text: A way of progressing agents' lack of cover

parts.note: to lope is to move along with a long bounding stride
the CIA is the American intelligence agency, home to secret agents

explanation.surface: Spies on the move with nowhere to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: Cover here is hair on the head, not a spy's cover story.
explanation.definitionFit: Alopecia is the medical term for hair loss, leaving the scalp bare.

clue.text: High-flying electronic equipment icon with visa difficulty

indicators.note: difficulty suggests the letters are in trouble and scrambled

explanation.surface: A celebrity's visa trouble stops a plane's systems.
explanation.definitionFit: Avionics are the electronic systems used in aircraft for navigation and control.

clue.text: Go out of one's way to look after knotted hair on calves

definitions.text: Go out of one's way to look after

indicators.note: knotted hair is tangled, so these letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Tending to matted hair on young cattle takes special effort.
explanation.definitionFit: To lavish care on someone is to give them generous attention, going beyond what is needed.

clue.text: Rough up the Spanish implement

parts.note: feeling rough is feeling sick

indicators.note: up in a down clue turns the Spanish word upwards, reading backwards

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Beating up the Spanish tool.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives SICKLE; its partner in 'hammer and sickle' is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickle is a curved hand tool for cutting grain, an agricultural implement.

clue.text: More than one artist in pull-out

indicators.note: in places the artist inside the scrambled letters
out signals the letters of pull are put out of order

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter featured in a fold-out supplement.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural is the grammatical form for more than one of something.

clue.text: Religious pictures one disregarded as frauds

indicators.note: disregarded means the letter for one is left out of the word

parts.note: icons are religious paintings, especially in the Orthodox church
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Sacred paintings once ignored turn out to be fakes.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives CONS; its partner in 'pros and cons' is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A con is a swindle, or informally the swindler, so cons can mean tricks or frauds.

clue.text: Ubiquitous wife has the lot: two cooks — everything

parts.note: having the lot means having all

indicators.note: cooks, as in cooking the books, means the letters of two are falsified into a new order

parts.note: everything means all

explanation.surface: A wife who already owns everything hires two cooks as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Wall-to-wall means covering every part, found everywhere, as carpet fills a floor.

clue.text: Hell with back to front relative darkness

indicators.note: back to front means the last letter is shifted to the front of the word

parts.note: Hades is the underworld of Greek myth, hell

explanation.surface: Hell, with its gloom, seen from behind.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay gives SHADE; its partner in 'light and shade' is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: Shade is an area shielded from direct sun, darker than its surroundings.

clue.text: Odd cure for linen that's unbleached

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of cure are in a strange order

explanation.surface: A strange treatment for linen left undyed.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is the pale greyish-yellow colour of raw, untreated linen or silk.

clue.text: Seal accepted a lot of money for getting close and personal

parts.note: to seal a deal is to clinch it
accepted, as in admitted, is in
a grand, a thousand pounds, is abbreviated G

explanation.surface: Settling a deal for a fortune gets things intimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Clinching means holding tight in a clinch, as boxers or lovers do in an embrace.

clue.text: Sea snail is more fresh by river

indicators.note: fresh suggests the letters of more are made anew in another order

explanation.surface: A sea creature is livelier beside fresh water.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an edible ear-shaped shellfish, a kind of abalone, found around the Channel Islands.

clue.text: Try to be a loveless, awful source of power

indicators.note: awful signals the letters are made into a dreadful jumble
love is zero, the letter O, so loveless drops an O from the word to

explanation.surface: An attempt to be an unloved, dreadful generator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loveless' takes O from TO, leaving T; 'awful' rearranges TRY, T, BE, A into BATTERY, whose partner in 'assault and battery' is entered.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery stores and supplies electrical power for a device.

clue.text: France's doomed people carrier?

parts.note: people carrier suggests a modern minivan, but here it is the cart taking the condemned to the guillotine in revolutionary France

explanation.surface: A French family car with no future.
explanation.walkthrough: 'People carrier' is a British term for a minivan; the clue really means the open cart that carried prisoners to execution during the French Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: A tumbril was the cart used to take condemned prisoners to the guillotine.
